e2ce8ac2de.q: How did MB Mentors sustain operations for seven years while offering most services for free?
e2ce8ac2de.a: MB Mentors initially self-funded with money from a group of founders. After about six months, they started their first CEO roundtable for second-stage businesses with revenues between $1 million and $50 million. The roundtables are the only service they charge for, and the revenue from these monthly 8 to 12-member groups meeting for 10 months of the year generates enough income to keep the volunteer organization operating. Since nobody on staff receives payment, the organization requires far less money to run than a traditional business with payroll and benefits.

e924aff1aa.q: Why did MB Mentors pivot from in-person to virtual operations in March 2020?
e924aff1aa.a: MB Mentors launched on March 6th, 2020 with the intent to meet mentees in person and conduct workshops and CEO roundtables. However, on March 11th, 2020, the pandemic hit, forcing the organization to quickly learn about Zoom and change their business model from in-person to virtual. While virtual access helped people contact them remotely without travel frustration, the team found that roundtables really require in-person dynamics, so they transitioned back to in-person meetings once restrictions lifted.
